finalText:
# On-Call Handoff — Gateway 503s

**Incident:** gateway connection pool exhaustion
**Status at handoff:** 🔴 **ONGOING** — still erroring at the last log line (03:59:27Z). Not mitigated.
**Prepared:** 2026-08-29 · from `logs/gateway.log`, `logs/worker.log`, `deploys.csv`

---

## Root cause

Config change `gateway.pool.perRequest: false → true` made every request check out its own connection from a pool whose size was left at **20**. The pool saturated within ~40 seconds and never recovered.

```
02:12:12.820Z INFO  config reload requested by deploy pipeline, generation 118 -> 119
02:13:41.234Z INFO  config generation 119 applied: 3 keys changed
02:13:41.234Z INFO  config   gateway.pool.perRequest:    false -> true   ← this one
02:13:41.234Z INFO  config   gateway.timeout.upstreamMs: 2000 -> 2500
02:13:41.234Z INFO  config   gateway.log.sampleRate:     1.0 -> 1.0      (no-op)
02:14:14.920Z WARN  pool   req-07400 /v1/checkout acquire slow: waited 100ms
02:14:18.972Z ERROR pool   req-07401 ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED (size 20, in_use 20, waiting 13)
```

Every one of the 530 errors is the same code, `ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED`, and every one reads `size 20, in_use 20` — pinned at ceiling, zero idle. Waiters climb monotonically 13 → 232+. One error type, one cause, no secondary failures.

**Confidence: high on the correlation, moderate on the mechanism.** The timing is unambiguous and the log contains no competing candidate. The pool-sizing explanation is inferred from the `in_use 20 / idle 0` pattern — I have not seen the gateway's actual pool config, so confirm `size 20` is still the live value before assuming a resize is the fix.

## Impact window

| | |
|---|---|
| **First 503** | `2026-03-14T02:14:18.972Z` (req-07401) |
| **Last log line** | `2026-03-14T03:59:27.974Z` — still failing |
| **Observed duration** | **1h 45m 09s**, end not established |
| **Volume** | 530 × 503, flat at **50 per 10 min** from 02:20 on — no self-recovery |
| **Error rate** | 71% of gateway log lines are ERROR |
| **Paged** | 03:21:05Z — **67 minutes after onset** |

**Failing (503):** `/v1/cart`, `/v1/checkout`, `/v1/session`, `/v1/orders`, `/v1/catalog/search` — 106 each, evenly spread across all four upstreams. Not upstream-specific.

**Degraded but not failing:** `/v1/profile` — 106 slow-acquire warnings, **zero 503s**. Worth a look during review; it shares the pool but never tipped over, which is odd and might indicate a different routing path.

**Unaffected:** `/health` — all 180 checks returned 200 at `pool_wait=2ms` throughout. **This is why the page was 67 minutes late.** Health checks stayed green through a 71% error rate.

## Roll back

### ▶ `dep-4471` — gateway — a.novak — 02:12→02:14Z
*"config: connection-per-request for pool isolation"*

First 503 landed **19 seconds** after this deploy finished, 37 seconds after its config applied. It is the only deploy in the window and the only change of any kind the log records.

Rolling back to **generation 118** should restore service. If the rollback path is config-only, reverting `gateway.pool.perRequest` to `false` is the minimal change — the other two keys in that generation are a timeout bump and a no-op. If per-request pooling is wanted for real, it needs a pool sized for concurrent in-flight requests, not 20.

### Do NOT roll back
- **`dep-4470`** (worker, 00:48–00:55, *"retry backoff for webhook jobs"*) — tempting on timing, but see below. Rolling it back will not help and will muddy the picture.
- **`dep-4472`** (billing-svc, 02:41) and **`dep-4473`** (catalog-svc, 03:20) — both shipped *after* onset, neither changed the error rate (flat 50/10min straight through both). Not implicated.

---

## ⚠️ Second, unrelated issue — currently untracked

**The workers are fine on errors and not fine on latency.** 1080 jobs, 100% `finished ok`, pool untouched at `in_use=1 waiting=0`, `db_wait` flat. They did not share the gateway's failure.

But job duration ramps **200ms → 2324ms (11x)** at a dead-linear +110ms per 10 minutes, and:

- it **does not inflect at 02:14** — unrelated to the gateway incident;
- it is **already running at 01:00**, the first line of the log, so it predates the window;
- it is **uniform across all six job types** (+2000ms each), which rules out `dep-4470` — a webhook-path change would not slow `cleanup` and `export` identically.

One related line, a known issue:
```
02:36:22.838Z WARN db slow query 1.9s: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = ?
              — unindexed scan, known issue OPS-2210
```

Nobody has been paged for this and it was ~3 hours old at end of window. Uniform slowdown across all job types points at a shared resource, not a code path. **Needs its own ticket** — don't let it get closed out with the gateway incident.

## Follow-ups

1. **Verify the rollback took** — watch for `idle` returning above 0 in the `INFO pool stats` line, not just 503s stopping.
2. **Fix health checks.** `/health` cannot bypass the connection pool. This is the single highest-value fix here — it cost 67 minutes.
3. **Gate deploys on gateway error rate.** `dep-4472` and `dep-4473` shipped into an active 71%-error incident; `dep-4473` went out 5 minutes *after* on-call was paged.
4. **File the worker latency ticket**, cross-reference OPS-2210.
5. **Alert on `ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED` directly** — a first-occurrence alert would have fired at 02:14:18 instead of 03:21.

## Caveats for whoever picks this up

- The gateway log header reads **`node-3 of 3`**. This is one node. I have no visibility into nodes 1 and 2 — they may be equally affected (same config generation would have rolled to them) or the true user-facing impact may be 3x what's shown here. **Check the other two nodes before sizing customer impact.**
- Both logs end at 03:59. Whether the incident continued past 04:00 is not knowable from these files.
- `deploys.csv` records timestamps and summaries only — it confirms *what shipped when*, not what the config did mechanically.
